title: Cover photoshoot: Double Fantasy by John Lennon and Yoko Ono | 1980
content:
The cover photography for John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Double Fantasy album was taken on 15 September 1980.

The photographer, Kishin Shinoyama, suggested that they go to Central Park. Shinoyama took shots of the couple on the corner of West 72nd Street and Central Park West, which appeared on the back cover. The front cover shot was taken in the park, near Bow Bridge.

After John and Yoko finished with the recording of the record, we decided to shoot the cover in the glow of sunset. I was watching their loving attitude, so I proposed to them the idea of the kiss and that photo was picked for the front cover of the album. It was shot at a bench in Central Park. The back cover photo was shot at the crossing street in front of the Dakota where John and Yoko were living.
Kishin Shinoyama
Starting Over, Ken Sharp

Kishin Shinoyama took more photographs of Lennon and Ono on 18 September.

We shot that photo with us kissing, which would go on to be used as the front cover of Double Fantasy and we thought it looked great. But we weren’t that sure about it. When we showed that photo to our record company they said, ‘No, no, the photo on the cover has to be John looking like a bachelor. We want a single photo of John on the cover. You can’t be kissing.’ So that’s when we decided we were gonna do it, because both of us were rebellious people. John said, ‘From now on, we’ll only take photos of you and me looking at each other.’
Yoko Ono
Starting Over, Ken Sharp
